subject: AI & Agents
title: Context Windows and Memory
description: Learn Context Windows and Memory in one minute.

hook.text: Tell a chatbot your name at the start. Fifty messages later, it's forgotten.

buildup.text: A context window is the chunk of text the model can see at once — its short-term memory.

discovery.text: GPT-4 started with 8K tokens. Now models handle 100K+. But there's always a ceiling.

twist.text: Even with huge windows, models pay less attention to stuff in the middle of long texts.

climax.text: Long-term memory requires external tools — databases, retrieval systems, user profiles.

quiz.question: What is a context window in AI?
options: The amount of text a model can process at once
A visual display of AI training progress
The time limit for generating a response

details.summary: A context window is the maximum amount of text an LLM can process at once. It acts as the model's working memory — anything beyond it is forgotten. Larger windows enable longer conversations but cost more.
details.whyItMatters: Context window size determines what an LLM can do. Short windows limit conversations and document analysis. Understanding this constraint explains why chatbots forget things and lose coherence.
takeaways: The context window is the maximum text an LLM processes at once
Information beyond the window is lost — the model has no true memory
Larger windows enable better performance but increase cost

faq.question: Why do chatbots sometimes forget earlier parts of a conversation?
faq.answer: When a conversation exceeds the context window, earlier messages are dropped. The model literally cannot see them anymore. It appears to forget, but it never truly remembered — it just processed them in order.

faq.question: How large are modern context windows?
faq.answer: Early models handled 2,000-4,000 tokens. Modern models like GPT-4 handle 128,000 tokens. Some models claim up to a million tokens. However, performance often degrades for information in the middle of long contexts.
